transcript.text: Otto, you were meant to clear the path, not bring it in. Breakfast is waiting.

transcript.text: Morning, grandmother.

transcript.speaker: grandmother
transcript.text: Bruno, your wife's waiting in the breakfast room.

transcript.speaker: Bruno
transcript.text: Is Sadie still angry?

transcript.text: You came home after midnight.

transcript.speaker: Bruno
transcript.text: I went for a walk.

transcript.speaker: Sadie
transcript.text: Then why do you smell like parmesan and rosemary?

transcript.speaker: Bruno
transcript.text: Sadie.

transcript.speaker: Sadie
transcript.text: Bella, your ex.

transcript.speaker: Bruno
transcript.text: She offered me a snack.

transcript.speaker: Sadie
transcript.text: And you stayed until midnight?

transcript.speaker: Bruno
transcript.text: It was very good cheese.

transcript.speaker: puppy
transcript.text: Dad, are you in trouble?

transcript.speaker: Bruno
transcript.text: Your mother and I are discussing breakfast.

transcript.speaker: Sadie
transcript.text: Penny, your father is changing the subject.

transcript.speaker: Penny
transcript.text: Then can I have his cheese?

transcript.speaker: Sadie
transcript.text: Yes, he's had quite enough.

transcript.speaker: grandmother
transcript.text: Grandmother, come back in. Penny's negotiating for your breakfast.

transcript.speaker: Bruno
transcript.text: Your brother Sebastian did the too. He'd steal breakfast without leaving his bed.

transcript.speaker: grandmother
transcript.text: My twin got the looks. I got the sausage.

transcript.speaker: Bruno
transcript.text: You were supposed to share it.

transcript.speaker: grandmother
transcript.text: We did. Then the kennel burned down.

transcript.speaker: Bruno
transcript.text: They never found him.

transcript.speaker: grandmother
transcript.text: He's dead, grandmother. You can't spend every morning waiting.

transcript.speaker: Bruno
transcript.text: You're allowed to miss him, Bruno.

transcript.speaker: grandmother
transcript.text: I do. That's why I can't keep looking at that.

transcript.speaker: Bruno
transcript.text: Wait. That smell from the grooming room...

transcript.speaker: grandmother
transcript.text: He used to hide in here as if I couldn't smell him.

transcript.speaker: grandmother
transcript.text: Fresh fur? No, I'm imagining it.

transcript.speaker: grandmother
transcript.text: Bruno, come and smell this.

transcript.speaker: grandmother
transcript.text: We heard you. What's happened?

transcript.speaker: Bruno
transcript.text: This smells like Sebastian.

transcript.speaker: grandmother
transcript.text: We all shed, grandmother. It's probably mine.

transcript.speaker: Bruno
transcript.text: I thought the too. Then I smelled it again.

transcript.speaker: grandmother
transcript.text: You really think he's been here?

transcript.speaker: Bruno
transcript.text: I don't know. I need you to look.

transcript.speaker: grandmother
transcript.text: I wish it were him. I do. But nobody survived that fire.

transcript.speaker: Bruno
transcript.text: Then whose scent is this?

Title card: BENEATH THE DOUBLE COAT - The Secret in the Snow

audience.retelling: In a snowy cabin, Bernese Mountain dogs converse in human speech about domestic disputes, breakfast, past relationships, and a missing twin named Sebastian who supposedly died in a kennel fire. Later, finding a pile of fresh fur in the grooming room sparks renewed debate over whether Sebastian might still be alive.

understood.claim: Otto tracked snow inside and is scolded by grandmother at the start
Bruno came home late smelling of parmesan and rosemary from his ex Bella
Sebastian is a missing twin who supposedly died in a kennel fire
A pile of fresh fur in the grooming room makes the dogs suspect Sebastian is still around

uncertainties.question: How do talking dogs operate in this snowy rural setting?

checks.evidence: Dialogue explicitly explains Sebastian, the kennel fire, and the lingering grief.
Finding the fresh fur and smelling Sebastian's scent directly triggers the investigation and debate among the dogs.
Sadie confronts Bruno about smelling like parmesan and rosemary after staying out late.
The belief that Sebastian died in the fire is challenged by the fresh fur and scent discovery.
Pacing smoothly transitions from domestic comedy to mystery and backstory without feeling rushed.
